open_points.subject: StaffProjectAssignment administrative reads
open_points.text: “An administrator manages staff accounts, assignments…” and “Created/modified by: administrator only.” The texts define assignment creation and revocation but no product action that reads or lists assignments.
open_points.question: Which product action, if any, lets an administrator read StaffProjectAssignment records, and may it read active assignments, revoked history, or both?
options: Administrator can list and/or retrieve active and revoked assignments.
Administrator can read only active assignments.
No product action exposes assignments after creation or revocation.
open_points.default_guess: Provide an administrator-only list containing active and revoked assignments.

witness.initial: An active operator has an active assignment to project P; another assignment for the same operator was previously revoked.
events: An administrator attempts to inspect the operator's project assignments before changing access.
outcomes: The administrator can read both the active assignment and the revoked assignment history.
No assignment-read product action exists, so the administrator cannot inspect either record through the product.
witness.observer: The administrator managing the operator's access.

open_points.subject: ServicePrincipal creation status
open_points.text: “status: PrincipalStatus (active | disabled)” and “the only modification is the status change active ↔ disabled” do not state which status create_service_principal assigns initially or whether the administrator chooses it.
open_points.question: Is a newly created ServicePrincipal active, disabled, or created in an administrator-selected status?
options: Every new principal is disabled until explicitly enabled.
The creating administrator chooses active or disabled.

witness.initial: No service principal exists for producer X.
events: An administrator creates a ServicePrincipal for X.
The administrator issues a credential and X immediately attempts an import.
outcomes: The principal was created active, so the credential can authenticate the import.
The principal was created disabled, so the import is blocked until a separate enable action.

open_points.subject: ServicePrincipal creation and first ServiceCredential
open_points.text: The texts separately say a ServicePrincipal is created by an administrator and a ServiceCredential is created by an administrator, while State 0 says credentials are “shown only at creation or rotation”; they never say whether creating a principal also mints its first credential.
open_points.question: Does create_service_principal atomically create and return an initial ServiceCredential, or must an administrator invoke a separate credential-issuance action?
options: Principal creation also mints one credential and returns its secret once.
Principal creation creates no credential; issuance is a separate action.
Principal creation optionally mints a credential at the administrator's request.
open_points.default_guess: Create the principal without a credential and require a separate credential-issuance action.

witness.initial: No identity or credential exists for producer X.
events: An administrator invokes create_service_principal for X and performs no further action.
X attempts to authenticate an import.
outcomes: Creation minted and returned an initial credential, so X can authenticate with it.
Creation produced only the principal, so X has no credential and cannot authenticate until the administrator separately issues one.

open_points.subject: Credential issuance while a ServicePrincipal is disabled
open_points.text: “re-enabling restores none of them, so a re-enabled principal needs a newly issued credential” does not say whether that new credential may be issued while the principal is still disabled or only after it is re-enabled.
open_points.question: May an administrator issue a ServiceCredential to a disabled ServicePrincipal, and if so does that credential become usable when the principal is re-enabled?
options: Issuance is refused while the principal is disabled.
A credential may be issued while disabled and becomes usable upon re-enablement.
A credential may be issued while disabled but is immediately revoked or otherwise never becomes usable.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse credential issuance until the principal is active.

witness.initial: Principal X is disabled and all of its earlier credentials have been revoked.
events: An administrator issues a new credential to X while X remains disabled.
X attempts an authorized import with that credential.
outcomes: Issuance while disabled was allowed; after re-enablement the new credential authenticates the import.
Issuance while disabled was refused, so X still has no usable credential after re-enablement.

open_points.subject: ProducerProjectGrant creation for an all_projects principal
open_points.text: “with [all_projects] … no project grant is consulted” and “with granted_projects every import requires an active ProducerProjectGrant” do not state whether the grant-creation action accepts an all_projects principal and stores an inert grant.
open_points.question: May an administrator create or revoke ProducerProjectGrant records for a ServicePrincipal whose scope_mode is all_projects?
options: Such grant creation is refused because grants belong only to granted_projects scope.
The grant is stored and audited but has no authorization effect.
The grant is stored and narrows or otherwise affects all_projects scope.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse grant creation for an all_projects principal.

witness.initial: Principal X is active with scope_mode all_projects, and Registry project P is active.
events: An administrator attempts to grant X project P.
The administrator later inspects X's access records.
outcomes: The action is refused and no ProducerProjectGrant exists because X already has global scope.
A ProducerProjectGrant is created and appears in X's records, although imports never consult it.

open_points.subject: ServicePrincipal administrative reads
open_points.text: The text defines ServicePrincipalView and says an administrator “manages … service principals,” but identifies only creation and status modification; it does not identify a product action for retrieving or listing principals.
open_points.question: Which product action, if any, lets an administrator read ServicePrincipal records, and does it include disabled principals?
options: Administrator can list and retrieve active and disabled principals.
Administrator can read only active principals.
No product action exposes principals after creation.
open_points.default_guess: Provide administrator-only list and detail reads for active and disabled principals.

witness.initial: Principal X exists and has been disabled.
events: An administrator attempts to find X in order to review or re-enable it.
outcomes: An administrative read returns X, including its disabled status.
No principal-read action exists, or disabled principals are omitted, so X cannot be found through the product.
